cornerCallouts: Riders will need to be precise through Turn 1, 'Expo 92', setting themselves up for the run down to Turn 2.
It's all about maintaining momentum through the fast, sweeping Turn 3, 'Michelin'.
'Dry Sack', Turn 5, is a crucial braking zone, a prime overtaking opportunity.
Turn 6, 'Nieto', requires a delicate touch, balancing speed and precision.
The riders will be threading the needle through the quick chicane of Turns 7 and 8, 'Peluqui'.
Turn 9, 'Curva Sito Pons', a sweeping right-hander that tests the rider's nerve and the bike's front-end grip.
'Aspar', Turn 11, is a critical corner for setting up the all-important final sector.
The final corner, 'Lorenzo', is a high-speed right-hander that leads onto the start/finish straight, where races can be won or lost.
strategyPoints: Tire management will be crucial on this abrasive Jerez surface, especially on the right-hand side of the tire.
The relatively short 4.423km lap means fuel consumption will be less of a concern than at longer circuits.
The pit lane is relatively short here, so a quick stop can make a real difference.
The flowing nature of the track means maintaining corner speed is key, requiring a setup that balances stability and agility.
With several heavy braking zones, brake fade could become a factor as the race progresses.
The long right-handers will put immense stress on the right side of the tires, forcing riders to adapt their riding style.
The slipstream effect is significant on the main straight, making for exciting overtaking opportunities.
A soft tire choice might offer an advantage in the early laps, but could degrade rapidly towards the end of the race.
weatherCommentary: The Jerez microclimate can be unpredictable, with sudden shifts in wind direction and temperature.
The Andalusian heat can be relentless, pushing riders and machines to their absolute limits.
The track temperature can soar rapidly in the afternoon sun, affecting tire grip and performance.
A sea breeze can sometimes roll in from the coast, bringing with it cooler temperatures and a welcome respite.
Rain is rare here, but when it does arrive, it can turn the race on its head, favouring the brave and the skilled.
